A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MURGAT study. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–E are readable and support reliable matching across the revision.

before.justification: v1 reports original human annotations, evaluator comparisons, and multimodal generation experiments on WorldSense and Video-MMMU, including reasoning-effort and programmatic-grounding analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds citation-placement analysis, alternative evaluator results, bootstrap analyses, and an author audit of entailment judgments.

M1.justification: The three-stage evaluation pipeline, MURGAT-SCORE computation, programmatic grounding variants, and prompts remain unchanged. Appendices A.5–A.6 explain existing citation handling; the inline-citation splitting rule was already present in v1’s Figure 9.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same audiovisual attribution and question-answering tasks using WorldSense and Video-MMMU. The added validation examines existing outputs without introducing another dataset, modality, population, or input scenario.

E2.justification: v2 Table 10 adds pipeline comparisons against Gemini-3-Pro-only, Gemini-2.5-Flash-only, and GPT-5.2/Gemini-2.5-Flash evaluator configurations. Appendix B.3 also newly reports Qwen3-Omni entailment-evaluator results. Existing generation baselines and earlier subtask comparisons are retained.

E3.justification: Added analyses introduce alternative evaluator assignments, automatic citation-placement classification over 600 annotated sentences, and author review of 50 randomly sampled entailment judgments. These are additional evaluation procedures; the original benchmark splits, metrics, and generation settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 substantially expands validation of the evaluation metric: citation-propagation checks in A.6, evaluator-choice and family-bias analyses in B.3, annotation-size sensitivity in B.4, and a manual error audit in B.5. These address reliability questions beyond v1’s retained decomposition ablations, reasoning-effort sweeps, and qualitative examples.

E5.justification: v1 reports point correlations and annotation agreement without confidence intervals. v2 introduces 10,000-resample bootstrap analyses, 95% confidence intervals, significance statements at p < 0.001, and subsampling intervals for 30, 50, and 80 responses (Tables 11–12). No increase in independent generation runs is stated.

E6.justification: Existing matched scores are unchanged, but v2 adds a substantial metric-validation result set. Table 6 reports 89 multi-citation sentences among 600, with 71 end-dumped cases; Table 10 adds alternative-evaluator Pearson correlations of 0.879, 0.830, and 0.757; B.5 reports 47/50 judgments matching the pipeline. Tables 11–12 add uncertainty and stability results.

T1.justification: The task definitions, citation verification formulation, and coverage, precision, recall, and MURGAT-SCORE equations are unchanged. Appendix A.5 provides a worked illustration of existing scoring rules, without introducing a new definition, theorem, or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions and claims: MURGAT, a human-correlated attribution metric, unreliable grounding despite correct answers, and trade-offs between reasoning and attribution. The additional validation supports these retained claims.

C2.justification: A.5–A.6 add explanations of partial credit for mixed-source citations and argue that citation propagation preserves rankings. B.3–B.4 interpret the added checks as evidence against evaluator-family bias and for sample stability; B.5 identifies ambiguous temporal boundaries in audit disagreements. Existing accuracy–grounding interpretations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Figure 2 now explicitly identifies the +CITATION setting and states that High thinking effort is the default configuration. A.6 describes citation-placement classification and clarifies the existing splitting rule. Prompts, programmatic implementation descriptions, and code/data access information are retained.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds MIRAGE (Martin et al., 2025), acknowledges its similar decomposition and verification pipeline, and distinguishes MURGAT through temporal, per-modality citations and separation of observable claims from reasoning. The discussion also names and more precisely characterizes the already-cited MCiteBench and MAVIS.

P1.justification: Changes include a localized related-work rewrite, additional explanatory and validation subsections in Appendices A–B, standardized Qwen3 names, wording corrections, and a conference publication notice. The main section sequence and most existing prose remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds four tables (6 and 10–12), expands Figure 2’s caption, and relocates or renumbers existing tables as content reflows. Existing plots, schematics, annotation screenshots, case-study figures, and prompt panels are retained without substantial redesign.

improvement.justification: The new confidence intervals, evaluator comparisons, and 50-judgment audit make the evidence for MURGAT-SCORE more informative than v1’s point correlations alone. Citation-handling explanations and the MIRAGE comparison also improve clarity. The gain remains limited: validation still rests on 20 input examples, and the pipeline comparisons retain Gemini-based entailment, so the added checks do not conclusively resolve broader reliability and family-bias concerns.
